label: rem:q-energy-terms-and-limits
title: The three energy terms, classical/deep-quantum limits, and crossing-energy relation
html:
This remark unpacks the three terms of the q-energy \mathfrak{E}_q(K) in the substrate action/mass chart of the categorical Hamiltonian, its classical and deep-quantum limits, and its distinction from the crossing energy.

The three terms.

  1. Rotational term J_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q: The q-deformed rotational contribution. For a spin-\frac{1}{2} state at the substrate parameter q, [1/2]_q [3/2]_q \cdot \hbar_q \approx 0.818 \times 0.0991 \approx 0.0811. This vanishes at q = 1 (where \hbar_q \to 0).
  2. Translational term p_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q / (2[n]_q): The q-deformed writhe kinetic contribution, with denominator [n]_q supplying the q-deformed strand inertia.
  3. Rest-action term \mathfrak{S}_q(K): The categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q = \mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{L}_q) evaluated on the static knot (\mathcal{L}_1 = 0), which coincides with the rest projection of the categorical Hamiltonian in the substrate mass chart (\ell_P = \hbar_q\,t_P = 1):
  \mathfrak{S}_q(K) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)).

At a single brane level, its magnitude equals |\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))| (categorical mass as Markov trace). Converting from the substrate mass chart to the causal-cone chart multiplies by c_q^2 = 1/(q - 1)^2, while dividing the electronic causal-cone rest energy \mathfrak{m}_e c_q^2 by the Planck tick t_P = q/(q - 1) yields the per-tick hadronic scale \mathfrak{E}_0 = \mathfrak{m}_e/\bigl(q(q - 1)\bigr). For torus knots (including the trefoil), the single-level trace is nonzero whereas the hyperbolic volume vanishes; the tower mass arises from quantum dilogarithm contributions across the brane tower (mass endomorphism conjecture).

Limits.

Limit \mathfrak{E}_q(K) (substrate mass chart)
q = 1 (classical) j(j+1) \cdot 0 + w^2 \cdot 0 + \mathfrak{S}_1 = \mathfrak{S}_1
q \to \infty (deep-quantum) J_q^2 \to q^{2j+1}, \; p_q \to w \cdot q, \; \mathfrak{S}_q \to \infty
Rest frame (p_q = 0, J_q = 0) \mathfrak{S}_q(K) = \mathfrak{m}(K) (rescaled to \mathfrak{m}(K)\,c_q^2 in the causal-cone chart)

Distinction from crossing energy.

Whereas \mathfrak{S}_q(K) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)) is a non-additive Markov trace invariant under braid conjugation and Reidemeister moves (up to framing), the crossing-level functional assigns q to each positive crossing and -q^{-1} to each negative crossing, with mean asymmetry \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \approx 0.1045 per crossing. Because q \neq q^{-1}, positive and negative crossings carry unequal Skein weights, providing the algebraic source of parity asymmetry before trace evaluation.
